 Order
They are heard.
Perused the case-diary/challan papers.

2] This is the applicant's second bail application filed under Section 483 of B.N.S.S./ 439 of Criminal Procedure Code, 1973, as he/ she is implicated in connection with Crime No.256/2024 registered at Police Station Tukoganj, District Indore (MP) for offence punishable under Sections 420, 409, 120-B, 467, 468 and 471 of IPC, 1860.
The applicant is in custody since 21.04.2024.
His first bail application M.Cr.C. No.34302 of 2024 was dismissed by this Court vide order dated 23.08.2024 on merits.

3] The allegation against the applicant is of embezzlement to the tune of Rs.7 Crores, as it is alleged that on the pretext of giving contract to the tune of Rs.737 Crores, the applicant got construction work worth Rs.5 Crores from the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:32329 2 MCRC-29445-2025 complainant Mukesh Jain, and the bank guarantee submitted by him worth Rs.2.37 Crores has also been encashed, and thereafter, the applicant has refused to pay the amount.
4] Counsel for the applicant, at the outset, has submitted that subsequent to the arrest of the applicant on 21.04.2024, the applicant's society, of which he was the Chairman, namely, Rani Durgawati Wardha District Adivasi Co-operative Sooth Girni Society, Yerla, Maharashtra has executed as many as six sale deeds in favour of the complainant worth more than Rs.15 Crores,
whereas, the total dues are not more than Rs.8 Crores.

sentences.text: Thus, it is submitted that in such circumstances, when the entire dues of the complainant have already been set off by the execution of the sale deeds, further custody of the applicant would not be necessary, who is lodged in jail since 21.04.2024, and final conclusion of trial is likely to take sufficient long time.

5] Shri Vivek Singh, learned senior counsel appearing for the objector has also submitted that it is true that the sale deeds have been executed, however, the bail may be allowed if the applicant and his family members, who are also the accused in the present case undertakes not to raise any dispute in any civil or criminal proceedings as to the execution of the said sale deeds subsequent to their release, as the present application is not being opposed only on the ground that the sale deeds have been executed, which have also been admitted by the applicant.

6] Shri Manu Maheshwari, learned counsel for the applicant, on the instructions received, has submitted that his client and his family members shall not raise any dispute in any civil or criminal proceedings as to the execution of NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:32329 3 MCRC-29445-2025 the sale deeds which have been executed in favour of the complainant by the said Society.
7] Counsel for the State, on the other hand, has opposed the prayer.
8] Heard.

On due consideration of submissions, on perusal of the case-diary, as also the documents filed on record, this Court is inclined to allow the present application, as the amount of embezzlement appears to have been settled by the applicant.
9] Accordingly, without commenting on the merits of the case, the application filed by the applicant is allowed.

The applicant is directed to be released on bail upon furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.25,000/- (Rupees Twenty Five Thousand) with one solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court for his/her regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that he / she shall remain present before the court concerned during trial and shall also abide by the conditions enumerated under Section 437 (3) Criminal Procedure Code, 1973.
10] M.Cr.C. stands allowed and disposed of .
